result.summary:
I took over from the predecessor's last commit f21537c in a fresh worktree via fast-forward; head b947e73 is the same as origin wip/v080-r2, and the tree is clean. The predecessor's code compiled and its tests passed. There was no lead commit "Stand beim Abbruch" to review.

What this run changed:
- The terrain showed stripes on slopes. The field pattern is now computed in the shader instead of read from a blurred texture, and fine detail fades out with the pixel's footprint.
- Arcade's two-tone grass bands were barely visible. The shader now draws them with sharp edges near the road.
- New render check `props_spiegel`: the props builder's mirrored MultiMesh nodes actually rendered.
- Stand-in sprites tuned to 0.8 / 1.15 (measured against Arcade).
- German docs in `docs/renderer-modern-gelaende.md`; report and pictures in `deliver/R2/`.

Full gates on b947e73 with a clean tree, all measured:
- `tools/run_tests.sh`: 592 unit tests and 76 checks OK, 0 failures, 630 s (one full run).
- `tools/golden.sh check`: 20 von 20 identisch.
- `tools/run_render_checks.sh modern`: 5 of 5 files OK.
- `modern_sight.gd`: F1–F3 and F7 green.

Terrain gate: 0.000 % magenta at T1–T4, S1 and C1. Ribbon tips on the inside of the same bend still overlap by up to 1.83 m. Three lines in the kernel fix this (measured, sight checks stay green). The kernel belongs to R1, so I did not apply them.

The terrain alone looks clearly better than Arcade. The whole Modern picture does not yet: the skeleton still lacks R1's and R3's content, and stand-ins are Arcade's own sprites.

contract_issues: Kernel: TerrainProfile cuts each row by its own curvature, so inner ribbon tips overlap (71 pairs, ≤ 1.83 m). Also cutting by _kappa() of the side (3 lines) gives 0, with modern_sight F1–F3 and F7 green (measured, reverted; the kernel belongs to R1).

'≤ 2 draw calls per prop set and chunk' conflicts with §4.6.6, which picks variants per prop, and with D24's second mirrored node: a 2-surface tree with two variants, or a baked+cutout house on both sides, needs 4 calls. Today 2 at most, measured.

F7 says 'no decorative vegetation'; renderer-modern.md §7.6 says relief, vegetation and buildings. I implemented the stricter reading; the lead should confirm whether scenery rocks and houses may stay in the corridor.

The terrain gate (≤ 0.2 % magenta below the horizon) is met as soon as the far-ground rim exists, because the rim closes everything below the horizon; ribbon holes show only in the far-ground share and the A/B pictures.

Arcade fogs sprites from close range towards a brightened fog colour (RoadRenderer._modulate). F4 forbids Modern to fog more, so mid-distance scenery is 7–16 % darker and more saturated than in Arcade (measured).
graphics.modern.props.bend_cover, bend_cover_max_h_m and graphics.modern.terrain.styles have their defaults in code; the graphics config section belongs to R1.
Leaving Modern = ModelDB.release_all() + ModernMaterials.drop_shared() still has no owner (A-4). The props builder releases its own share with release_all(self).

result.look_verdict:
Judged against the Arcade frame of the same simulation state. The Modern frame here has only the skeleton (debug road, built-in light, sky gradient) plus R2.

Better: the terrain. There are real hills and valleys: at T1 the road visibly winds over the hills, T2 and T3 show crests and slopes. Fields in the scenery's colours have sharp edges, the mown verge shows Arcade's two grass tones as bands, and there is gravel, a ditch, water under the C1 bridge, snow at N1 and wetness at R1. I found no void, no visible ribbon edge and no underside. The card oaks are finer than Arcade's sprites and cast real shadows.

Same: 83 of 86 prop sets are still Arcade's sprites as billboards. They are flat, turn with the camera, and are 7–16 % darker than in Arcade.

Worse: the insides of bends are bare by rule F7. At T2, 38 of 135 props are missing; at T4 the big cliff and pine are gone. Fields fade into a uniform tone beyond about 270 m. The horizon is only fog colour because the backdrop is R1's.

Overall, the Modern frame is not yet clearly better than Arcade: it lacks R1/R3 content (markings, guardrails, mountains and clouds, vehicles, signs). The terrain on its own is clearly better.

I took over the stopped predecessor's work in a fresh worktree (fast-forward to a8ec8b8) and reviewed the commit the lead had made without review. All 241 scripts compile and the 61 race3d unit tests pass. The only defect: the check_modern_stage "nacht" check depended on random traffic; it now runs on a fixed scene. I then finished R1:
- New render checks check_road_parity and check_light_base.
- A cold-cache shader warm-up tool, warmup_cold.gd. It found 5 HUD shaders that were compiled only after the loading screen. The session now hands the HUD its start state behind the loading cover, so they compile during loading.
- The kernel's stand-in terrain (debug_road.gd) now uses the scenery's grass colours; it was 15 % darker than Arcade.
- Documentation (§10 of renderer-modern.md) and the report (bericht.md).

result.look_verdict:
The road in Modern is as good as Arcade's or better. It has wheel tracks, grain, patches, crisp anti-aliased paint, real W-beam guardrails with posts and soft contact shadows, and Arcade-exact line positions.

At dusk Modern is clearly better: the low sun glares on the asphalt, rails and edge line. Night and dawn match Arcade's mood and add the low beam on the 3D rails and retro-reflective lines. The wet road in rain is convincing, with the bright sky reflected towards the horizon.

As a whole picture, Modern is NOT better than Arcade yet. Without trees, wind turbines, houses, stations, vehicles and signs (R2, R3 and later builders), every daytime frame is emptier. The ground is a flat stand-in band, and at noon the sky has no sun disc because the sun stands behind the car. S2 (no fuel station), S4 (no city or bridge) and S5 (no finish gantry) are visibly bare. Only the merged picture (RINT) can show whether Modern is 'deutlich besser'.
